text:
git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(spl): a throwable the RUNTIME built still reported line 0

`new SplFixedArray(-1)` answered `getLine() === 0` where php answers the line of the `new`.
Zero is not a line php ever prints, and it takes the uncaught report's whole location tail
with it.

Two halves, and each was wrong on its own.

The throw sequences in the SplFixedArray and doubly-linked-list runtimes write every field
of the Throwable payload — class id, message, length, code, previous — except the creation
line, which they left as whatever the allocator had put there. `emit_throwable_creation_line_unknown`,
the shared helper for the same situation, stored an explicit zero. Both now read the line
published at the call into the builtin, which is php's own rule: the `new` lives in the
runtime and has no php line, so php names the CALL.

The gate deciding which calls publish was the other half. It asked whether the class's
emitted BODIES were synthetic — the right question for a class built from a synthesized
PHP AST and the wrong one for `SplFixedArray`, which has no PHP body at all. It now reads
the class's own DECLARATION span: a compiler-injected class carries `Span::dummy()`, and
that is one hash lookup instead of a scan of every emitted method.

MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6 — a negative size, a negative `setSize()`, an out-of-range
offset write, `intdiv(1, 0)`, and a plain user `new` — all five lines now agree.
